implementation_statement: The ticketing vendor provides user management, but SYS-01 has one account: the owner's administrator account, also used by the fill-in technician. Gap: no named account for the fill-in technician, no account review, and (found in P07) the account was still signed in on the fill-in technician's personal phone weeks after the last cover day. Named, limited fill-in account by 2026-09-30.
evidence: SYS-01 user list and active sessions page (P07 test)

responsible_role: Ticketing and POS vendor; owner assigns roles
implementation_statement: SYS-01 enforces role-based access to tickets, customer records, reports, and exports. The owner will assign the fill-in technician a role without export or settings rights.
evidence: SYS-01 role settings; vendor SOC 2 report (P09)

implementation_statement: The laptop locks after 5 minutes, the tablet after 2 minutes, and the phone after 1 minute. Gap: the bench PC has no password and never locks, and it sits behind a half wall the counter can see. Password and 5-minute lock by 2026-09-15.

The shop Wi-Fi uses WPA2 with a password. Gap: one network for business devices, the card terminal, customer devices under repair, and customers' phones; the password is posted on the wall. The router supports a separate guest network that has never been turned on.

The owner has no security training beyond repair forums. The owner will complete a free small-business cybersecurity course, read the P2PE Instruction Manual (PIM), and take a phishing refresher every year, starting by 2026-11-30.
evidence: Course certificate and PIM read date (planned)

implementation_statement: SYS-01 logs sign-ins (with device and location), ticket views, and customer list exports for 90 days. The productivity suite and processor portal keep their own sign-in histories.
evidence: SYS-01 activity log screen; vendor SOC 2 report

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Nobody has ever reviewed the SYS-01 activity log or the email sign-in history. From 2026-10, on the first Tuesday of each month, the owner reviews sign-ins and exports in SYS-01 and the email and processor sign-in histories, and notes the review in the security log.
The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: no device-return procedure or sealed emergency access sheet if the owner is unavailable (due 2026-12-31).

provider_if_inherited: Ticketing and POS vendor; productivity suite provider
implementation_statement: The ticketing vendor backs up SYS-01 (RPO 1 hour, RTO 4 hours in its SOC 2 system description) and the productivity suite keeps file versions. Owner responsibility: working copies of open data recovery jobs on the bench PC have no second copy, and the owner keeps no export of SYS-01 data.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; bench PC review

implementation_statement: Named accounts exist for the owner in every service and for the bookkeeper in the accounting SaaS. Gap: the fill-in technician signs in to SYS-01 as the owner, so the activity log cannot tell the two apart.
evidence: SYS-01 user list; accounting user list

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite provider; payment processor; accounting SaaS; bank
implementation_statement: MFA is on for the productivity suite, accounting SaaS, bank portal, and processor portal (all owner administrator accounts). Gap: MFA is off on the SYS-01 administrator account (turned off so it could be shared) and on the camera account. Both on by 2026-09-15, after the fill-in account exists.

The owner keeps unique passphrases in a password manager. Gaps: the router administrator password is the factory default, and the SYS-01 password was never changed after the fill-in technician last used it.
evidence: Password manager vault review; router settings

implementation_statement: No incident log, reporting time, or contact list existed. P08 sets same-day logging of every suspected incident and lists who must be told (processor within 24 hours of suspecting a card data compromise; Florida notices within 30 days of determination).
The account takeover runbook (P08) was adopted on 2026-08-31 with a contact list. Gap: the contacts are not printed and the runbook has not been walked through (due 2026-09-30).

Recycled devices and scrap parts go to a certified recycler with a certificate per lot. Gaps: drop-off devices get a factory reset only when time allows, with no record per device and no verification; transfer drives are never wiped between jobs. SP 800-88 Rev. 2 procedure with a per-device log by 2026-10-31.
The storefront is locked and alarmed (monitored) when closed. Devices in custody are kept in a locked cabinet overnight. Customers stay on the counter side of the half wall.
First risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Reviewed every July and after a major change.

The processor's merchant agreement and the ticketing vendor's terms and SOC 2 report are on file. Gaps: no vendor list; no confidentiality agreement with the fill-in technician; the recycler contract has no data terms; the AI assistant runs on consumer terms with training on.

The provider router has a built-in firewall and blocks unsolicited inbound traffic; the laptop host firewall is on. Gap: customer devices under repair share the internal network with the bench PC, tablet, and terminal. Separate guest and bench networks by 2026-10-31.

provider_if_inherited: Ticketing and POS vendor; payment processor
implementation_statement: SYS-01, SYS-03, SYS-04, and the processor portal use TLS. Card data is encrypted in the P2PE terminal before it leaves it.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; P2PE solution listing

implementation_statement: The ticketing vendor encrypts data at rest (inherited). The laptop has full-disk encryption; the tablet and phone are encrypted by their passcodes. Gap: the bench PC and the two transfer drives are unencrypted and hold about 1.6 TB of customer data.
evidence: Vendor SOC 2 report; device encryption status (P07 test)

provider_if_inherited: Ticketing and POS vendor; device OS vendors
implementation_statement: The vendors patch their SaaS. Automatic OS updates are on for the laptop, tablet, phone, and bench PC. Gap: the router firmware has never been updated.
Built-in antivirus with real-time scanning and automatic updates runs on the laptop and bench PC. Owner responsibility: keep it on and scan any customer drive before opening files.

No retention rule exists. Passcodes and account passwords stay in ticket notes forever, and transfer and recovery copies are never deleted. POL-01 section 8 sets deletion of passcodes at release and of customer data copies 14 days after delivery; the historical purge is due 2026-10-31.
evidence: P03 SYS-01 search 2026-07-20; bench PC listing
